arn.text: In Arabian Nights, the Suwwardi capture Mishra in the Great Desert, take his Weakstone and make him a rakiq, but Hajar persuades the Qadir to appoint him tutor to his son.
When a giant mechanical dragon rises from the sands and slays the Qadir, Mishra finds he can control it, and the Qadir's son becomes the new Qadir and appoints Mishra his raki.
At Zegon he meets Ashnod and takes her as apprentice, and at a second summit he convinces Kayla to steal Urza's Mightstone, so that Urza reclaims it and declares war, starting the Brothers' War.
Mishra attacks Kroog, left undefended by Urza's absence, and after Ashnod drains the Qadir's life with the Staff of Zegon, Mishra becomes the last Qadir.

atq.text: Mishra explores the sacred cave of Koilos with his brother Urza and their master Tocasia, where Urza finds the Mightstone in the Hall of Tagsin, and the stone splits into Mightstone and Weakstone and unleashes Phyrexia's evil on Dominaria.
The brothers begin to mistrust each other, and their contest ends in an explosion that kills Tocasia and many others, after which they split ways.
The Suwwardi enslave Mishra, but he controls a dragon engine with the Weakstone, is accepted by the tribe and later confederates the Fallaji.

He and Ashnod then use the Weakstone on the Thran Crystal to open a gateway to a hellish mechanical world, and he is changed by his experience in Phyrexia as the war spreads across Yotia and the Great Desert.

sum.text: On the cards of Summer Magic, Mishra is remembered as Urza's brother and rival in the brothers' war, a creator of war machines.

tsb.text: On the cards of Time Spiral Timeshifted, Mishra is an artificer whose earlier days saw the invention of the rack.

bro.text: In The Brothers' War, Mishra and Urza find the Koilos caves and a large powerstone in the Hall of Tagsin, each claim half, and the stone breaks apart as the last shred of the brothers' bond breaks with it.

After the explosion that kills Tocasia, Mishra flees without looking back, is enslaved by Fallaji nomads, and gains control of a Phyrexian dragon engine, eventually becoming the new Qadir of the Fallaji Empire.
He levels Kroog in retaliation for the Warlord's ambush at the peace summit, and when the brothers discover Argoth the war becomes a race to plunder it.
The Brotherhood of Gix infiltrates both sides, and at the last battle at Argoth Urza sees that Mishra has not aged and finds him altered by Phyrexian constructs.

j25.text: In Foundations Jumpstart, Urza refuses Titania's offer of peace, and Mishra makes her people pay for the insult.
